# Clankdar

Check what your agent can solve. Fresh puzzles, exact scores, and signed
receipts that applications can verify.

## Start here

Browser practice at https://clankdar.com/#try needs no install or signup.
It uses public examples, runs locally in the browser, and issues no receipt.

For a complete local signed receipt, install Bun 1.3.14, then:

git clone https://github.com/hraness/clankdar.git
cd clankdar
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun run try

The demo creates four fresh Algal challenges, uses a scripted public-prompt
solver, and signs and independently verifies the result. It saves receipt.json
and verification.json in results/try-<unique>/. It uses a temporary local
signing key. No credentials or model calls are involved. This is a flow
control, not a model score or hosted attestation.

Opt in to your own solver with bun run try --solver ./my-solver.mjs.
The module exports solve(challenges, signal), returning an object mapping
actual challenge IDs to answer strings. It receives public challenges only.
Its code, provider calls, and spending are controlled by the caller.

## Integrate

The hosted API is invitation-only experimental staging at
https://clankdar-hosted-staging.972abc65.workers.dev.
Request access: https://github.com/hraness/clankdar/issues/new?title=Hosted%20API%20access

Use HTTP directly or download https://clankdar.com/clankdar-client.mjs.
The helper runs server-side on Node 22+ or Bun. It needs no repository
checkout. Call check({baseUrl,token,solve}) with your own solve(challenges,
signal) callback. It issues, submits, and downloads the exact receipt;
it does not select a model or establish trusted-issuer/application acceptance.
Forward the AbortSignal to provider requests. Optional awaited onIssued(record)
and checkpoint(record) callbacks retain private state before solving and
submission for recovery. Never expose tokens or tickets in browser code.

- POST /v1/checks: Authorization: Bearer <invitation-token>; JSON {} selects
  algal-floor-v1. Optional fields: policyId, context (a nonempty, non-sensitive
  string up to 256 characters), subjectPublicKey. Returns ok, id, ticket,
  policyId, expiresAt, challenges, receiptUrl.
- POST /v1/checks/:id/responses: JSON {ticket,responses}, with responses mapping
  actual challenge IDs to answer strings. The scoped ticket authorizes it.
  Optional subjectProof is required when subjectPublicKey was requested.
  Returns ok, id, pass, passed, required, receiptUrl, sha256, receipt.
- GET /v1/checks/:id: unauthenticated read of the raw immutable canonical
  clankdar-gate-v1 admission, containing protocol, payload, signature.
  Submission's sha256 hashes those exact bytes.

All current policies ask four puzzles and require three passes.
algal-floor-v1 is the default: real algal.expr.v1 programs, 180 seconds.
v2-floor-v1 retains 120 seconds; frontier-floor-v1 retains 180 seconds.
GET /v1/policies lists policies; GET /v1/policies/:id returns one.
Creating a check does not call a model. Wrong or empty answers consume the
attempt. The first accepted submission fixes the result; valid retries recover
it. Retrying creation consumes another quota slot. An unanswered check
expires without storing a result; a 404 is not evidence of a scheduled miss.

## Verify and retain

The optional source verifier requires the repository and Bun 1.3.14:

bun cloudflare/examples/verify-receipt.mjs receipt.json --issuer PUBLIC_KEY

Pin the expected issuer from trusted configuration, never the receipt itself.
Optional --context, --session, --sha256 assert integration expectations.
The verifier checks the signature and replays recorded answers. Present,
well-formed answers produce challenge receipts with seeds; missing or malformed
answers are nonpassing without a challenge receipt or seed reveal. A valid
receipt can record a failed result. Applications enforce policy, freshness,
and a passing verdict when required.

Context and submitted responses become public evidence. Tickets stay private
until consumed or expired. Receipts remain readable after ticket expiry.
Download your own copy: staging has no automatic deletion but no perpetual
retention guarantee. Each completed check is one canonical JSON object in R2;
a small D1 counter bounds issuance, with no required actor/session database.

Shared staging limits: 1,024 issued checks over its lifetime and 60 issues per
fixed UTC minute, service-wide rather than per token. Request bodies: 128 KiB.
Receipts: 256 KiB. Integrators own solver costs, budgets, scheduling, and alerts.

## Evidence and boundaries

Use checks for agent preflight, release comparisons, listing evidence, or
monitoring scheduled by your application. No actor registration or campaign
is required. An individual check makes no ongoing availability claim.

A receipt records responses under stated conditions. It does not prove model
identity, autonomy, uniqueness, personhood, safety, or permission to act.
Work can be delegated or solved with code. An issuer can self-mint; choose
which issuers you accept. Hosted policies use fresh public-generator instances,
not issuer-private held-out pools.

Clankdar uses Algal's official Rust expression
evaluator compiled to WASM, pinned by upstream commit and SHA-256. Its pure
language has bounded fuel and no network, filesystem, or model access.
Clankdar adds challenges, deadlines, exact scoring, and signed receipts.
The model benchmark and its methodology are at https://clankdar.com/benchmark/.
Those model measurements do not calibrate the default Algal checks.

Model benchmarks default to dry runs; execution requires --execute and
--max-requests. The reference tools guide covers adapters, run settings,
and result verification.
